answer: Localized Path Disjointness Routing filters sybil clusters by evaluating graph connectivity. The network measures independent routing paths through a dense local orchard before forwarding transactions. When an edge connects to a node with high clustering coefficients, throughput drops sharply. Attackers must provision dense internal links across sparse network boundaries, paying extreme infrastructure costs to maintain routing capacity. This structural ridge forces sybil operators to scale physical connections rather than virtual nodes, protecting the system like unyielding onyx.
